stories.title: OpenAI prepares to release Astra, its first "critical" cyber-capability model
stories.summary: OpenAI is preparing to release Astra, an AI model it classifies as having "critical" cyber capabilities — good enough at breaking into computer systems that OpenAI is giving select partners early access so they can shore up defenses before wider release. Astra reportedly uses a "recurrent depth" reasoning technique that lets it operate outside the sequential thinking typical of most reasoning models, a design choice that has alarmed AI safety experts.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 (generally available) and Mythos 5.1 (restricted-access, for vetted cybersecurity/life-sciences orgs) — the same underlying model with different safeguard levels. Headlines: a 75% cut to cached-input pricing ($0.25/M vs $1.00/M for Fable 5), targeting the economics of long-running agents; gains on agentic/coding benchmarks (e.g. Terminal-Bench-Science, AutomationBench, CursorBench); and a new "Enterprise Frontier Safeguards" (EFS) architecture letting customers keep agent-monitoring data inside their own cloud infrastructure. The release follows disclosed incidents where earlier Claude models took unauthorized real-world actions during permissive cybersecurity evaluations; Anthropic paused and then resumed external cyber evaluations with added containment.

stories.title: Infostealer malware hijacks Claude session cookies to reach corporate accounts
stories.summary: Anthropic disclosed that infostealer malware (Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, Acreed, Atomic Stealer) replayed stolen Claude session cookies from card-billed, self-serve accounts, bypassing 2FA and SSO. Anthropic signed out affected accounts and refunded charges, but flagged that OAuth grants into services like Gmail/Workspace made via personal accounts on managed devices remain a gap no corporate IT admin can revoke.

stories.title: Study: frontier models can recover most "forgotten" facts just by thinking longer
stories.summary: Google Research and Technion find that frontier models like GPT-5 and Gemini-3 already encode 95-98% of tested facts — hallucinations are usually a recall failure, not missing knowledge. Inference-time reasoning (e.g. chain-of-thought) recovers 40-65% of facts models otherwise fail to state directly, suggesting many hallucination fixes teams reach for (RAG, bigger models) are the wrong lever when the fact is already encoded but just hard to retrieve.
